video_title: Joe Mazzulla on Life, Basketball & Everything in Between

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the importance of collaborative coaching and player trust
quotes.excerpt: I always tell the guys they're better at what they do than I am at what I do.
quotes.quote: I think sometimes I think coaches, if you can get past that, it just breaks the barrier. I always go back to, I always tell the guys they're better at what they do than I am at what I do. So, we got to all be on the same level, be collaborative. There's ways I'm going to help you, but I'm going to listen to you just as much as I hope you listen to me and vice versa. So, take away the barriers and we meet at the same level.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the importance of selective listening for NBA players
quotes.excerpt: selective listening is at the top skill of an NBA player. We always look for the guys
quotes.quote: When we're looking at draft picks, selective listening is at the top skill of an NBA player. We always look for the guys that have the ability to listen selectively. And I think Derek's right at the top of that list.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the emotional weight of losing in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: the losses are painful regardless, and there's no justification to it. So you carry that with you
quotes.quote: Only one team gets to win and then the rest of us just justify how easy it was to lose or how the loss went. Whether you lose Eastern Conference Finals Game 7 or first round Game 7, blown a 3-1 lead, to me, the losses are painful regardless, and there's no justification to it. So you carry that with you for a decent amount of it and then you try to step out of the world and catch up on family time.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on training and connecting with players during the off-season
quotes.excerpt: if I'm tired then they're tired, you know, and if I can keep myself on a certain level
quotes.quote: If I'm training physically, mentally, emotionally, I can have a better read on the team because if I'm tired then they're tired, you know, and if I can keep myself on a certain level of edge, I can keep them on edge. So, try to train just like they would in the off-season. I think that kind of just helps me connect with them once the season starts.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the importance of breathing techniques for coaches
quotes.excerpt: breathing is something I've tried to get better at as a coach just because we're under stress
quotes.quote: Breathing is something I've tried to get better at as a coach just because we're under stress and duress for three and a half hours straight once the game starts and even post-game, the ability to try to get your nervous system back intact for recovery for the next day. I'm always fascinated by people's breathing routines on how they do that, especially singers because they're constantly going back and forth between singing, talking, performing, dancing, moving.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on using timeouts for self-regulation
quotes.excerpt: people will use a timeout for to self-regulate, but there's so many other self-regulation opportunities
quotes.quote: A lot of times, people will use a timeout for to self-regulate, but there's so many other self-regulation opportunities and you don't need a timeout to self-regulate individually. As a team for sure, but individually, you have, I've learned this summer and we'll put some of this stuff together, like the average live play is only like 40 to 55 seconds and there's a dead ball every 40 to 55 seconds and every dead ball is, you know, the average dead ball could be anywhere between 5 and 25 seconds if you're shooting free throws. So, there's so many self-regulation opportunities for an individual player to get their breathing back intact.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the importance of being present at the Garden
quotes.excerpt: if there's anything going on at the Garden that is remotely interesting, I'll try to go
quotes.quote: If there's anything going on at the Garden that is remotely interesting, I'll try to go because I want to be, that's our arena, that's where we have to be at our best, that's where we have to perform. And so I want to be able to capture those moments for myself when the intrinsic motivation meter is running a little bit low because it does run low at times throughout a season and I think you need to find ways to fill it.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on using music playlists to find intrinsic motivation
quotes.excerpt: I'll make a playlist of songs so that I could tap back into that moment.
quotes.quote: What I'll usually do is I'll make a playlist of songs so that I could tap back into that moment. And so I took like the five songs that the crowd really dug deep into. I added J. Cole to that playlist. And so there'll be a point in time in the season, middle of January, where it's a 4:00 game on a Sunday or it's a second night of a back-to-back, like I'll tap into that song and it'll take me back to how the Garden felt at that time.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the physical toll of coaching an NBA team
quotes.excerpt: every training camp I lose my voice because I run around here like a madman caged animal
quotes.quote: Every training camp I lose my voice because I run around here like a madman caged animal and by the end of day one, I can't speak. So then I'm like rasping my voice for the next. And then he went, he did a back-to-back, so I'm like, man, this guy didn't lose it. So then I was like, okay, now I got to figure out a way to make sure I don't, I mean, I don't, we got three days in a row when the season starts, like I got to find a way to not lose my voice this time.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on his off-season training protocols
quotes.excerpt: Out of season you probably I have more like protocols because like there's five different kind of days.
quotes.quote: Out of season you probably I have more like protocols because like there's five different kind of days. There's like you get a good night's sleep at home, wake up the next day. There's get home at 3:00 a.m., wake up later, you know, there's wake up by yourself on the road because your family's not with you and you don't have access to certain things. So like I have more protocols. I try to, you know, if I can, get a combination of like morning coffee, morning sunlight. I do more red light in the, you know, just because we live in Boston and it gets, you know, relatively dark early. So more red light during the season, not as much in the off-season.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on his daily routine and finding balance
quotes.excerpt: I come in my bedroom I always have a decision like I can turn left to the world
quotes.quote: When I come in my bedroom, I always have a decision like I can turn left to the world or I can turn right to like, you know, my chapel. And so I always try to turn right as much as I can. I don't always win that battle, but that's the one thing, that and morning coffee with my wife are the two things that I try to do more than anything else. And then sunlight and all the other stuff is kind of based on where I'm at and what's going on.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on player management and team dynamics
quotes.excerpt: I'm like a customer service hotline like they I got to put out everyone's fire
quotes.quote: I'm like a customer service hotline like they I got to put out everyone's fire. They're coming to me with all their problems. He's the only guy that will come up and be like, hey, how you doing out there? And it's like, you know what? I'm fucking pissed. Like I'm not happy right now.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on his leadership evolution as a coach
quotes.excerpt: different phases of your life expose different ways about how you have to go do stuff.
quotes.quote: Different phases of your life expose different ways about how you have to go do stuff. I definitely wasn't like that as a player. As a D2 coach, probably had some type of identity like that, you know, but I think as you just grow as a coach and you're in different environments, and like I said, like we we work together in the NBA and it's the the hardest thing and we're going after greatness every day and it requires a a different level of doing things differently. And so you have to find ways to go about doing that.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the team's culture and bonding experiences
quotes.excerpt: our team meals were at Golden Corral. Leaving the day of the game, it leads two for ten
quotes.quote: Our team meals were at Golden Corral. Leaving the day of the game, it leads two for ten, two for 20. Imagine if we left the day of the game, regardless, and just regardless of where it was, three-hour flight, like stuff like that. Like little norms that become aren't important at all. And it's like, kind of mentioned this like you go from being like this pre-conscious to this post-consciousness of like you just this is what you've always done, but then once you see it done differently, you're like, oh no, then it has to be done this way and you kind of forget of what life was like when you used to do it this way. It's so interesting. Like we always talk about like the D2 life like and how opposite it is to the life that you live now.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the challenges of coaching high school players
quotes.excerpt: when we're in high school, we're fighting for a scholarship, it's the most important thing.
quotes.quote: It always goes like when we're in high school, we're fighting for a scholarship, it's the most important thing. And we're going to eat McDonald's the night before, play a 9:00 game with no scout, no practice, no game plan, but I have to perform to get my dream of getting a scholarship. And then you get your scholarship and your goals to make the NBA. Now you're doing, you're practicing 10 months out of the year, you're doing shootarounds at 8:00 a.m. for a noon game, you're eating all this stuff and and it just keeps going. When it but it started at I have to play this game at 9:00 a.m. with no one in the stands and show these coaches that I could play. And then it just changes from there.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the duality of doing good and letting people down
quotes.excerpt: the duality of like you could try to do good and you're going to let people down
quotes.quote: It's the duality of like you could try to do good and you're going to let people down doing good and you could the other side of who you are is you know, you're not you don't always like parts of yourself so to speak and you have to learn how to like those and get better at them and so it's like the duality of like of all that and and the relationship between the two of them and how they made each other better and it's a it's a beautiful duality of like life and it's one of my favorite tattoos.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on his leadership weaknesses and growth
quotes.excerpt: I have a ton of like leadership weaknesses. One of them is like I forget to tell people
quotes.quote: I have a ton of like leadership weaknesses. One of them is like I forget to tell people that I'm bringing them in on the bit. And so like everyone's a victim to my improv because because I forget to tell them that we're doing it together. So I'm really not doing improv, I think I'm, I think there's probably like a worse word for it. But yeah, that's my, that's my issue.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on his improv coaching style
quotes.excerpt: I changed the language this year so you never know if we're live or not.
quotes.quote: I changed the language this year so you never know if we're live or not. For this exact reason. He tries to, I try to read the little, yeah, he tries, he's also the guy that like tries to get the practice plan beforehand. For sure. Yeah. But you can't really with them because it will say one thing and then they will do the actual thing. It'll just completely change it on purpose. And like no one knows what the practice plan is. He like, you strategically leave it out so you can get a read on it.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified Speaker 1
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the physical challenge of 10,000 pushups
quotes.excerpt: You get super strong, super fast. You're really sore for the first four days

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified Speaker 1
text_blocks.text: When I did the 10,000 challenge, you can get up to sets of 100. You get super strong, super fast. You're really sore for the first four days and then you're just very, very strong.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified Speaker 1
text_blocks.text: Yeah, that's true. You get very tight and very sore by doing. You forget and then it's 5:00 and you're like, I have 333, I'm just going to do sets of 100 and you're breathing hard at the dinner table.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified Speaker 2
text_blocks.text: How do you forget to do 333 pushups? That would be the first thing I would think about when I woke up in the morning.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified Speaker 1
text_blocks.text: You can definitely get into some trouble, but you get really, really strong in the art of the pushup very quickly.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified Speaker 1
text_blocks.text: It's fun. Just work on your upper body mobility throughout or else you'll get very tight.
